skill.name: commit-prepare
skill.description: Prepare conventional git commit messages by reviewing local status, staged diffs, and unstaged changes before user-confirmed commits.
skill.summary: Drafts conventional commit messages and supports safe staging and commit confirmation.
skill.author: ByronWilliamsCPA

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives around examples, commit templates, or attribution links. I confirmed limited external-command risk where the skill instructs staging and committing files, especially the heredoc command substitution for multi-line messages. No prompt injection or covert network behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution for commit messages
remediation.suggestion: Replace heredoc command substitution with a safer workflow, such as writing the message to a temporary file and using git commit -F after confirmation.
Default to staging explicit files and require an extra warning before git add . when changes include secrets, generated files, or unrelated work.
State that git add and git commit must run only after showing the exact files and final message to the user.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages takes time and can miss project context. This skill reviews staged changes and drafts conventional commits with safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Runs local git status and diff commands to inspect staged and unstaged changes.
Classifies changes into conventional commit types, scopes, and breaking change markers.
Drafts subject, body, and footer text for conventional commit messages.
Asks before staging files or executing git commit commands.
Suggests separate commits when unrelated changes appear in one worktree.
Adds Claude Code attribution when requested by the workflow.
limitations: Requires a local git repository and command-line access.
Cannot infer business intent that is absent from the diff.
May stage unintended files if the user approves broad staging.
Does not validate remote policies, CI status, or code ownership.

use_cases.title: Prepare Daily Commits
use_cases.description: Turn a worktree diff into a concise conventional commit message before committing.

use_cases.title: Review Release Changes
use_cases.description: Summarize staged release changes and mark breaking changes before a release commit.

use_cases.title: Split Mixed Work
use_cases.description: Identify unrelated file groups and propose separate commit messages for each group.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Message
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has already staged files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest a conventional commit message. Show the subject, body, and any footer.

prompt_templates.title: Stage Specific Files
prompt_templates.scenario: A worktree has both related and unrelated edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my unstaged changes, group related files, and ask me which group to stage before drafting a commit.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Breaking Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: A change may affect public behavior or data formats.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staged diff, identify any breaking API or data changes, and draft a conventional commit with the correct marker.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Multiple Commits
prompt_templates.scenario: A branch contains several logical changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all current changes, split them into logical commits, propose staging groups, and prepare messages for each commit.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add token refresh and tests.
output: Suggested type: feat with auth scope.
Body: Explains automatic refresh and test coverage.

output_examples.input: The worktree includes parser fixes, export changes, and documentation updates.
output: Recommended split: parser fix, export feature, and documentation update.
Each group receives a separate conventional commit message.
The user chooses which group to stage first.

output_examples.input: A staged API change modifies the response envelope.
output: Suggested type: feat with breaking change marker.
Footer notes that clients must update response parsing.
The final message is shown before any commit command runs.

best_practices: Review the staged diff before approving any commit command.
Stage specific files when the worktree contains unrelated changes.
Check for secrets, generated files, and large binaries before staging.
anti_patterns: Do not approve broad staging when the worktree contains unknown files.
Do not bypass hooks unless a maintainer explicitly accepts the risk.
Do not use the skill to rewrite pushed history without review.

faq.question: Does this skill commit automatically?
faq.answer: No. It should show the proposed message and wait for confirmation before committing.

faq.question: Does it support conventional commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps changes to conventional commit types, scopes, bodies, and footers.

faq.question: Can it split one worktree into several commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify unrelated changes and suggest separate staging groups.

faq.question: Will it push changes to a remote?
faq.answer: No. It may suggest pushing, but pushing should remain a separate user decision.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets?
faq.answer: It asks the assistant to check for credentials, but users should still run project-specific secret scans.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
